name: FedEx Corporation
description: FedEx Corporation provides a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce and business services through companies operating collaboratively, including Federal Express Corporation, FedEx Ground and FedEx Freight.
businessModel: FedEx generates revenue by providing global express delivery, small-package ground delivery, and less-than-truckload (LTL) freight services. It is currently undergoing a massive network consolidation known as 'One FedEx'.
geopoliticalSummary: FedEx is exposed to global trade fluctuations, particularly in China and the Middle East. Geopolitical conflicts in the Red Sea impact its logistics segment through rerouting and increased costs.

revenueByGeography.note: Exact segment name from filing: 'United States'
Includes all operations outside the U.S.

keySuppliers.name: Boeing
keySuppliers.strategicNote: Primary supplier for fleet modernization (777F and 767F).

keyCustomers.name: Diverse Customer Base
keyCustomers.strategicNote: No single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue.

commodityDependencies.note: Significant exposure to energy price volatility.

regionalExposures.note: Subject to trade tensions and regulatory compliance in China. Verbatim from 10-K: 'Our business and operations in China are subject to complex local laws... changes in trade policy and tariffs could adversely affect our results.'

Geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East affect the FedEx Logistics segment. Verbatim from 10-K: 'Geopolitical conflicts... including those in the Middle East, can lead to increased operational costs and rerouting of shipments.'

infrastructureDependencies.name: Memphis World Hub
infrastructureDependencies.note: Central hub for global express operations.

sources.name: FedEx 10-K FY2024
sources.verbatimQuote: The United States and other governments have imposed and may further impose export controls and other trade restrictions.

name: United Parcel Service, Inc.
description: UPS is one of the world's largest package delivery companies and a leading global provider of specialized transportation and logistics services.
businessModel: UPS operates through three segments: U.S. Domestic Package, International Package, and Supply Chain Solutions. It manages a global network of aircraft and ground vehicles.
geopoliticalSummary: UPS faces geopolitical risks in the Red Sea and through its China-to-U.S. trade lanes. It has significant exposure to European markets and regulatory risks in China.

revenueByGeography.note: Includes U.S. Domestic and portions of other segments.
Europe is the largest international region.

keySuppliers.name: Airbus
keySuppliers.strategicNote: Major provider of aircraft for the international fleet.

keyCustomers.name: Amazon
keyCustomers.strategicNote: Amazon and its affiliates represent 11.8% of consolidated revenue.

commodityDependencies.note: Significant operational dependency on energy markets.

regionalExposures.note: Largest international region. Verbatim from 10-K: 'Europe accounted for approximately half of our International Package segment revenue.'
Diversions around the Red Sea increase costs. Verbatim from 10-K: 'Geopolitical instability in the Red Sea... increases logistics costs and transit times.'

sources.name: UPS 10-K FY2024
sources.verbatimQuote: Geopolitical instability in various parts of the world, including the Red Sea, has impacted and could continue to impact our business.

name: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd.
description: ZIM is a global container liner shipping company with a leading position in niche markets where it believes it has a competitive advantage.
businessModel: ZIM operates an asset-light model, primarily chartering vessels to provide container shipping services across major global trade routes.
geopoliticalSummary: As an Israeli-headquartered company, ZIM is uniquely exposed to the Red Sea crisis. It has rerouted most services around Africa, significantly increasing costs and transit times.

revenueByGeography.note: Significant presence in Asian regional trade.

keySuppliers.name: Seaspan Corporation
keySuppliers.strategicNote: Primary provider of chartered vessels, including new LNG-fueled ships.

keyCustomers.name: Global Retailers
keyCustomers.strategicNote: Serves major global retailers for Transpacific imports.

commodityDependencies.note: Exposure to global fuel price volatility and rerouting costs.

regionalExposures.note: Directly targeted by Houthi attacks. Verbatim from 20-F: 'We have rerouted most of our services around Africa... increasing transit times by 10-14 days and significantly increasing costs.'
Verbatim from 20-F: 'Our business and operations are subject to risks associated with the security and political situation in Israel.'

infrastructureDependencies.name: Cape of Good Hope Route
infrastructureDependencies.note: Primary alternative to Suez Canal due to Red Sea crisis.

sources.name: ZIM 20-F FY2024
sources.verbatimQuote: The rerouting of our vessels around Africa has resulted in increased transit times and higher operating costs.

name: Matson, Inc.
description: Matson is a leading provider of ocean transportation and logistics services in the Pacific, with a focus on Hawaii, Alaska, Guam, and expedited services to China.
businessModel: Matson earns revenue through ocean transportation services and third-party logistics. Its high-margin 'CLX' expedited service from China to the US is a key driver.
geopoliticalSummary: Matson is highly dependent on the US-China trade lane for its expedited services. It is protected by the Jones Act in its domestic markets but faces competition in international routes.

revenueByGeography.note: Includes Hawaii, Alaska, and Guam services.
Primarily driven by expedited China services (CLX/MAX).

keySuppliers.name: SSA Terminals
keySuppliers.strategicNote: Crucial JV partner for West Coast terminal operations.

keyCustomers.name: E-commerce Retailers
keyCustomers.strategicNote: Uses expedited services for time-sensitive e-commerce imports.

regionalExposures.note: Verbatim from 10-K: 'Our China service is subject to risks from changes in trade policy and tariffs... geopolitical tensions could lead to trade restrictions.'

infrastructureDependencies.name: Port of Long Beach
infrastructureDependencies.note: Primary US gateway for China expedited service.

sources.name: Matson 10-K FY2024
sources.verbatimQuote: Abrupt shifts in trade policy or new tariffs could impact Trans-Pacific trade volumes.

name: GXO Logistics, Inc.
description: GXO Logistics, Inc. is the world’s largest pure-play contract logistics provider, offering technology-driven supply chain solutions for global blue-chip companies.
businessModel: GXO generates revenue through long-term contracts for warehouse management, order fulfillment, and reverse logistics. It specializes in highly automated facilities.
geopoliticalSummary: GXO is heavily exposed to European and UK markets. Geopolitical risks include labor shortages in the UK and regulatory shifts in the EU regarding ESG and employment.

revenueByGeography.note: Largest single market; boosted by Wincanton acquisition.
Includes significant operations in the Netherlands and France.

keySuppliers.name: Locus Robotics
keySuppliers.strategicNote: Strategic automation partner for warehouse fulfillment.

keyCustomers.name: Global Omnichannel Retailers
keyCustomers.strategicNote: Retail segment represents nearly half of total revenue.

commodityDependencies.note: Operational risk from rising wages and labor shortages.

regionalExposures.note: Verbatim from 10-K: 'Our operations in the United Kingdom represent a significant portion of our consolidated revenue... subject to local economic and regulatory conditions.'

infrastructureDependencies.name: Global Warehouse Network
infrastructureDependencies.note: 1,030 facilities globally forming the core of the business.

sources.name: GXO Logistics 10-K FY2024
sources.verbatimQuote: The United Kingdom is our largest single market by revenue.
